KnowledgeBase.title: Knowledge Base
KnowledgeBase.subtitle: How Poisik scores a design, and what each category is actually looking for.
KnowledgeBase.howScoringWorksDesc: Every analysis gets an overall score from 0 to 100, built from the six category scores below. Alongside the score, each issue found is tagged with one of three severities:
KnowledgeBase.criticalDesc: Usability or accessibility problems worth fixing immediately.
KnowledgeBase.warningDesc: Noticeable inconsistencies or missed best practices.
KnowledgeBase.suggestionDesc: Polish-level improvements — nice to have, not urgent.
KnowledgeBase.codeFixNote: Where a fix is concrete enough to express in code (a color, spacing, or type value), the issue includes a copy-pasteable snippet on the report page instead of just a description.
KnowledgeBase.visualHierarchyDesc: How clearly the design guides the eye toward what matters most. Primary actions, headlines, and key information should stand out through size, weight, contrast, and placement — not compete with everything else on the screen.
KnowledgeBase.visualHierarchyTip1: Give each screen one dominant call-to-action
KnowledgeBase.visualHierarchyTip2: Size and weight text according to its importance, not habit
KnowledgeBase.visualHierarchyTip3: Group related elements tightly, separate unrelated ones clearly
KnowledgeBase.contrastDesc: Whether text and interactive elements are legible against their background — both for general readability and for WCAG accessibility compliance.
KnowledgeBase.contrastTip1: Aim for at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio for body text
KnowledgeBase.contrastTip2: Don't rely on color alone to convey meaning (add icons or text)
KnowledgeBase.contrastTip3: Re-check contrast separately in light and dark states
KnowledgeBase.spacingDesc: Consistency and rhythm in padding, margins, and gaps. Cramped or uneven spacing reads as unpolished even when every individual element is well designed.
KnowledgeBase.spacingTip1: Use a consistent spacing scale (e.g. 4 / 8 / 16 / 24px) instead of arbitrary values
KnowledgeBase.spacingTip2: Give related elements less space between them than unrelated ones
KnowledgeBase.spacingTip3: Don't let touch targets crowd each other on mobile layouts
KnowledgeBase.typographyDesc: Font choices, sizing scale, line height, and hierarchy — whether text is easy to scan and comfortable to read at every size it appears in.
KnowledgeBase.typographyTip1: Limit a single screen to 2–3 font weights
KnowledgeBase.typographyTip2: Keep body text line length between 45–75 characters
KnowledgeBase.typographyTip3: Use a defined type scale instead of ad-hoc font sizes
KnowledgeBase.accessibilityDesc: Everything beyond contrast: alt text, visible focus states, touch target size, and whether the interface works for people using assistive technology.
KnowledgeBase.accessibilityTip1: Every interactive element needs a visible focus state
KnowledgeBase.accessibilityTip2: Touch targets should be at least 44×44px
KnowledgeBase.accessibilityTip3: Icon-only buttons need an accessible label, not just a tooltip
KnowledgeBase.consistencyDesc: Whether components, patterns, and interactions repeat predictably across the interface, instead of reinventing the same button or flow differently on every screen.
KnowledgeBase.consistencyTip1: Reuse the same button, badge, and card styles everywhere they apply
KnowledgeBase.consistencyTip2: Keep icon style consistent (stroke width, fill, size)
KnowledgeBase.consistencyTip3: Match interaction patterns app-wide (e.g. how every modal closes)

Support.title: Support
Support.subtitle: Need help? Check the answers below, or reach out directly.
Support.faqQ1: What image formats can I upload?
Support.faqA1: JPG, PNG, and WebP, up to 10MB per screenshot — the same limits shown on the New Analysis page.
Support.faqA2: Yes. Every analysis is private by default and only visible to you. It's only reachable by anyone else after you explicitly click "Share Report" on that report's page.
Support.faqQ3: Can I cancel my plan anytime?
Support.faqA3: Yes — manage or cancel your subscription anytime from Settings → Billing, via the Stripe customer portal. No lock-in period.
Support.faqQ4: What happens if an analysis fails?
Support.faqA4: If an analysis fails partway through, the credit it would have used is refunded automatically — you won't lose a slot on a failed run.
Support.emailUsSuffix: — we usually reply within a day.
Support.kbExplains: The Knowledge Base explains each category and how scoring works.

About.metaDescription: The story and mission behind Poisik, the AI-powered design audit platform.
About.title: About Poisik
About.intro: Poisik was built on a simple belief: every product deserves an expert design review, not just the ones with a design team on staff.
About.p1: Great UX/UI design is judged on hundreds of small decisions — contrast ratios, spacing rhythm, type hierarchy, accessibility affordances — that are easy to get wrong and expensive to get reviewed. Most teams either skip that review entirely or wait weeks for a senior designer's attention.
About.p2: We built Poisik to close that gap. Upload a screenshot or point us at a live URL, and our AI design auditor delivers the kind of structured, actionable critique a senior product designer would give — visual hierarchy, contrast, spacing, typography, consistency, and accessibility — usually in under a minute.
About.p3: Poisik isn't meant to replace designers. It's meant to give every team, regardless of size or budget, a fast first pass so the humans in the room can spend their time on the decisions that actually need judgment.
About.speedDesc: Design feedback is most useful before you've shipped, not after.
About.specificityDesc: Generic advice doesn't fix anything — every finding comes with a concrete recommendation.
About.accessibilityDesc: A design that only works for some users isn't a finished design.

Blog.title: Blog
Blog.subtitle: Notes on design systems, accessibility, and what we're learning building Poisik.
Blog.post1Title: Why contrast ratio is the highest-leverage design fix you can make
Blog.post1Excerpt: A one-line color change is often the single biggest accessibility and readability win available to any product team. Here is how we prioritize contrast findings in every audit.
Blog.post2Title: The design review most teams skip — and how to automate it
Blog.post2Excerpt: Spacing rhythm and typographic hierarchy rarely get dedicated review time. We break down what a senior designer actually looks for, and why it is teachable.
Blog.post3Title: Building Poisik: designing an AI critique that designers trust
Blog.post3Excerpt: Getting an AI model to give feedback that reads like it came from a senior designer, not a linter, took more prompt iteration than we expected.

Careers.title: Careers
Careers.intro: We're a small team building the design-review tool we always wished we had. There are no open roles listed today, but we're always happy to hear from people who care about design quality and craft.
Careers.p1: Poisik is early — which means the next few hires will shape how we build product, talk to users, and think about design quality at scale. If that sounds interesting, reach out and tell us what you'd want to work on.
Careers.noOpenPositionsDesc: Check back later, or follow our blog for updates on when we start hiring.

CookiePolicy.metaDescription: How Poisik uses cookies and similar technologies.
CookiePolicy.title: Cookie Policy
CookiePolicy.section1Body: Poisik uses a small number of essential cookies to keep you signed in and to remember your preferred language. These cookies are required for the service to function and cannot be disabled while remaining signed in.
CookiePolicy.sessionCookiesDesc: keep you authenticated across pages so you don't have to sign in repeatedly.
CookiePolicy.preferenceCookiesDesc: remember settings like your selected language (English or French).
CookiePolicy.section3Body: Our payment provider may set its own cookies during checkout to process your subscription securely. We do not use third-party advertising or tracking cookies.
CookiePolicy.section4Body: Most browsers let you block or delete cookies through their settings. Because Poisik relies on essential cookies for authentication, blocking them will prevent you from staying signed in.

PrivacyPolicy.metaDescription: How Poisik collects, uses, and protects your data.
PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPolicy.section1Body: When you create an account, we collect your name, email address, and authentication details. When you use Poisik to analyze a design, we process the screenshots or URLs you submit, along with the resulting analysis, in order to generate and store your reports.
PrivacyPolicy.section2Body: We use your information to provide and improve the Poisik service: authenticating your account, running design analyses, storing your project history, processing billing through our payment provider, and communicating important account or service updates.
PrivacyPolicy.section3Body: Screenshots and designs you upload are used solely to generate your analysis and are stored under your account so you can revisit past reports. We do not use your uploaded content to train third-party AI models, and we do not sell your content or personal data to anyone.
PrivacyPolicy.section4Body: We rely on trusted third parties to operate Poisik, including cloud hosting, database storage, payment processing, and AI providers used to generate design critiques. These providers only receive the data necessary to perform their function.
PrivacyPolicy.section5Body: You can export or permanently delete your account and all associated data at any time from your account settings. Deletion removes your projects, analyses, and personal information from our systems.
PrivacyPolicy.section6Body: Questions about this policy or your data can be sent to our support team through the contact options listed on this site.

TermsOfService.metaDescription: The terms that govern your use of Poisik.
TermsOfService.title: Terms of Service
TermsOfService.section1Body: By creating an account, you agree to use Poisik only for lawful purposes and only to analyze designs and content you own or have permission to submit. You are responsible for the content you upload.
TermsOfService.section2Body: Poisik offers a Free plan with a limited number of monthly analyses, and paid Pro and Team plans billed monthly through our payment provider. Upgrades, downgrades, and cancellations can be managed from your account settings at any time. Paid plans renew automatically until canceled.
TermsOfService.section3Body: Design critiques on Poisik are generated by AI models and are provided as guidance, not as a guarantee of design correctness, legal compliance, or accessibility certification. You remain responsible for reviewing and validating any changes made based on our recommendations.
TermsOfService.section4Body: You may not use Poisik to submit content that is illegal, infringing, or that you do not have the right to analyze. We reserve the right to suspend accounts that abuse the service, attempt to circumvent usage limits, or interfere with the platform's operation.
TermsOfService.section5Body: Poisik is provided on an "as is" basis. While we work to keep the service available and reliable, we do not guarantee uninterrupted access and are not liable for losses resulting from downtime or service interruptions.
TermsOfService.section6Body: We may update these terms as the product evolves. Continued use of Poisik after an update constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

ApiDocs.metaDescription: Programmatic access to Poisik's AI design analysis engine.
ApiDocs.title: API Docs
ApiDocs.subtitle: Programmatic access to Poisik's AI design analysis engine.
ApiDocs.authBody: Requests are authenticated with an API key, sent via the x-api-key request header. Access is currently available by request — reach out via Support to get one.
ApiDocs.endpointDesc: Submit a screenshot (as a URL or base64) and get back the same structured audit Poisik generates in the app — an overall score, per-category scores, and a list of issues with recommendations and, where possible, a ready-to-use code fix.
ApiDocs.imageUrlDesc: A publicly reachable image URL. Poisik downloads and resizes it server-side.
ApiDocs.imageBase64Desc: A base64-encoded image, sent directly. Pair with an optional mimeType (defaults to image/png).
ApiDocs.modelDesc: Optional — "groq" (default) or "gemini", which AI provider to use.
ApiDocs.error502: Couldn't fetch the image at imageUrl
ApiDocs.needKeyDesc: API access is available by request — reach out via Support to get one.
